title: Dallas Fed Texas Service Sector Outlook Survey (Oct 2026 data) — 9:30 a.m. CT / 10:30 ET on day 1 of the Oct 27–28 FOMC, the only 2026 edition whose data lands while the Committee is in the room
source: EST: dallasfed.org's own Texas Service Sector Outlook Survey page (dallasfed.org/research/surveys/tssos), fetched direct 2026-09-15 with a desktop user-agent (HTTP 200, 42,451 bytes) and quoted VERBATIM from its own markup. The table headed `2026 Release Dates` carries the column headers `Survey Period` and `Release (9:30 a.m. CT)` and the row `October | Tuesday, Oct. 27`, alongside the publisher's caveat that `The publishing process begins at 9:30 a.m. CT` and that it `cannot guarantee the exact timing all survey content becomes available online`. 9:30 a.m. CT = 10:30 ET. Independently corroborated from the publisher's own report archive: the September 2020 report (dallasfed.org/research/surveys/tssos/2020/2009, HTTP 200, read direct today) states `Next release: October 27, 2020` — and 2020 is this series' exact calendar twin for 2026 (identical August field window `August 18–26`, identical September release date Sept 29, identical October release date Oct 27, all four quoted from their own documents). Estimate on the two limits this lane records and neither of which any source quality can clear: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (`FED:` is scoped to federalreserve.gov's FOMC calendar, bottleneck #3117), and this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-15
notes: PROPOSED 2026-09-15 by the dallas-fed-tssos-2026-09-29 initial-research adjacency sweep. WHY IT IS A GAP AND NOT A DUPLICATE: this calendar carries the September (canonical as of today), November and December editions of this monthly series and skips October entirely — the same hole the dallas-fed-mfg-2026-09-28 lane closed on the manufacturing side hours earlier, which proposed its twin at 2026-10-26 (proposals/dallas-fed-mfg-2026-10-26.from-dallas-fed-mfg-2026-09-28.json). The manufacturing half of the October pair is now proposed and the services half was the missing one. WHY IT EARNS A ROW BEYOND SERIES COMPLETENESS, and this is a ground no other 2026 edition of this survey has: 2026-10-27 is day 1 of the Oct 27–28 FOMC meeting (fomc-2026-10-28, `high`, `confirmed`, titled `FOMC decision (meeting Oct 27–28)`), so this is the only 2026 edition whose data reaches the Committee's table while it is in session and inside its own blackout — and with the mfg twin at 10-26 the pair brackets the meeting's opening. It is also the only untracked date in this series that inherits the confound the 09-29 research measured: 2026-10-27 is the last Tuesday of October, which is the Conference Board's Consumer Confidence slot at 10:00 ET, 30 minutes ahead of this survey's 10:30 — the same structure that made all six SOURCED prior September editions rank a median 79.2nd-percentile |open→close| magnitude that belongs to the co-scheduled print rather than to the survey. Leaving 10-27 untracked leaves the next window-arithmetic pass reading a 10-27 tape as clean when it is not. THE PRIOR DECLINES ARE RECORDED AND NAMED: both dallas-fed-tssos-2026-12-01 (2026-09-05) and dallas-fed-tssos-2026-12-29 (2026-09-09) explicitly declined to file the 09-29 and 10-27 editions, on the ground that `filing further low rows for a series this doc has just measured as market-neutral would contradict the finding`. That research argument is correct and this proposal does not contest it — nothing here makes this survey more tradeable. The row is filed on calendar hygiene, exactly as the 12-29 row was, and strengthened by a structural fact the earlier declines did not have in hand. Read-it-do-not-trade-it: `symbols: []`, `low` impact, `estimate` date.
